question.problem: Given that the random variable $X∼\text{Exp}(\frac{2}{5}),$ calculate $P(X>7\,|\,X>2).$
question.worked_solution:
Given a random variable $X∼Exp(\lambda ),$ and two positive real numbers $s,t,$ the memoryless property of the exponential distribution states that

$$
P(X>s+t\,|\,X>s)=P(X>t)={e}^{-\lambda t}.
$$

In our case, we have $\lambda =\frac{2}{5},$ $s=2,$ and $s+t=7.$ From this, we can find $t$ as follows:

$$
t=(t+s)-s=7-2=5
$$

Substituting these values into the above formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X>7\,|\,X>2) & ={e}^{-\lambda t} \\  & ={e}^{-(2/5)\cdot (5)} \\  & ={e}^{-2} \\  & =\frac{1}{{e}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$
